Noise levels shift rules
This section explains one way of working
Companion Animal Travel Desk: cabin noise and pet lounge handling

This section sets the basic flow for moving animals, checking space, and keeping the lounge calm while flights turn over. Use it when passenger movement is active and the ground team is handing carriers between services. Keep talk brief, keep doors shut when possible, and watch for signs that a pet is stressed or the carrier is damaged.

When a traveler arrives with a companion animal, confirm the booking record, check that the carrier is secure, and move the animal through the handoff path without delay. If the animal needs a quiet pause, place it in the pet lounge only after the basic checks are done. <<FACT F022>> Do not promise special treatment that the desk cannot support, and do not send an animal onward until the carrier, label, and routing details line up. If there is any mismatch, stop the transfer and call the senior coordinator before the animal leaves the desk.

The lounge is a shared working space, so staff must keep noise low, avoid sudden movement, and keep food, loose straps, and open bags out of the aisle. Clean hands and clean surfaces matter more than speed. If a pet shows distress, separate the case from the main flow and use the calmest available route. <<FACT F005>> Record the handoff, note any visible issue, and pass the update to the next shift in plain language, not shorthand.

Travelers should be guided to wait clear of carrier lanes, and the desk should avoid crowding near the lounge door. If a pet arrives from a wet apron, check the carrier base before it is set down inside. If a carrier is marked for special care, treat it as priority handling and keep the chain of custody simple. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty lead if a case falls outside these rules.
